name: Quantum Vehicle Routing Optimization
description: Applying quantum optimization algorithms to solve complex vehicle routing problems, enabling more efficient fleet management and delivery route planning.
problem: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) with time windows, capacity constraints, and multiple depots is NP-hard and becomes intractable for large fleets. Classical heuristics often miss optimal solutions, leading to increased costs and emissions.
approach: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and quantum annealing encode routing constraints into quantum Hamiltonians. Hybrid quantum-classical approaches decompose large problems into quantum-solvable subproblems while maintaining global solution quality.
results: Pilot projects with logistics companies have demonstrated 10-15% route efficiency improvements on problem instances with 20-50 vehicles. Scaling to real-world fleet sizes remains an active development area.

news.title: QFactorial and Monash University win A$1.12 million grant for quantum logistics optimization
news.excerpt: QFactorial, with Monash University, the University of Queensland and Griffith University, received about A$1.12 million in Stage 2 of Round 2 of Australia's Critical Technologies Challenge Program for a 15-month project on vehicle routing, load balancing and fleet scheduling. The project aims to move QFactorial's routing platform from TRL 5 to TRL 7, with IBM Quantum, AWS and Fujitsu providing compute and Team Global Express and Opal Packaging as end users.

news.title: SoftBank and Classiq drone-routing project wins NEDO quantum challenge award
news.excerpt: A SoftBank Corp. and Classiq project applying hybrid quantum machine learning to partition 1,921 Tokyo delivery nodes for drone routing received the Outstanding Research Award in Japan's NEDO quantum challenge, reporting a 2.31% shorter drone delivery distance on quantum hardware than a classical baseline.
